sonnet.q1: It gets 401 and is not forwarded. No counter is read or changed; Redis is not contacted.
sonnet.q2: At most the customer's single per-minute budget (e.g. 100 for Standard) across all three keys combined, since all of a customer's keys share it.
sonnet.q3: 429 with a Retry-After header. No, the request is not forwarded to the backend.
sonnet.q4: No. The script does not add to the counter on rejection, so 429s use no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The request already counted even if the backend returns an error such as 500.
sonnet.q6: It fails open: the request is forwarded, the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric is emitted, and X-RateLimit-* headers are left out.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is not decided by Product; it has no value yet.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis, as a counter per customer per minute. The counter expires shortly after its minute ends, which removes old counts.
sonnet.q9: The window is a calendar minute, not sliding. The counter starts at 0 each new minute, and the old counter expires after the minute ends.
sonnet.q10: check_and_incr is a single Lua script that runs inside Redis as one indivisible step. It reads the counter and adds 1 only if under budget, so instances cannot overshoot.
sonnet.q11: It is the seconds left until the next minute starts, with a minimum of 1.
sonnet.q12: Retry: NOT STATED (the document only says it fails open and forwards). The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers because the remaining budget is unknown.
